mathematical_scope.main_result: For each fixed k>=2 the global deficit bounds rho times squared Gaussian label distance, uniformly over every d>=k-1 on a qualitative small positive interval. Equality of stability holds on the simplex orbit. In smaller dimensions the qualitative comparison is strict.
mathematical_scope.local_result: For balanced partitions near the simplex orbit, the deficit bounds any fixed fraction c<2/k of the exact loss against the closest moment reference, and controls the squared orbit distance times rho.
mathematical_scope.proof_review: Source-aware internal audit checked the additive covariance comparison and its singular endpoint, balance and rank, the symmetric facet estimate and rotational gauge, normalization of measurable transfers, and the tensor Hermite bound. The local proposition now expressly states balance and d>=k-1. Near maximizers in the proof overview are defined on the o(rho) scale.
mathematical_scope.computation: None is used in the mathematical proof.

mathematical_dependencies.input: Zhang, Equal Gaussian cells: the sharp simplex first-moment theorem
mathematical_dependencies.locator: Frozen preprint Sections 2–5; adapted with attribution in Proposition 2.1.
mathematical_dependencies.scope: The paper includes the covariance argument along an additive ray and the deductions for localization.
k=n+1 positive equal-mass full-rank polyhedral cells, sum of Gaussian interface areas. The k=2 trace-one covariance comparison is a singleton.
The Gaussian density of x-u is jointly log concave and the facet is a fixed convex integration domain. The zero-dimensional case has zero covariance.

bibliographic_audit.Gaussian_model: Isaksson–Mossel Conjecture 1.4(i) gives the balanced positive Gaussian formulation. Theorem 1.10 supplies the discrete connection, which is context in the paper.
bibliographic_audit.three_cells: Heilman–Tarter Theorems 1.9–1.10 give prior structure and three-cell context. Heilman arXiv:2306.03312v3, Theorem 1.5, states the explicit balanced Gaussian interval 0<rho<=0.1082 and a planar radial-mass deficit. Neither is an input to the proof.
bibliographic_audit.priority: The cited theorem statements were compared with the article. No priority claim is made.

isolated_pdf_only_reading.supplied_context: Fresh task with PDF paths and the five reader questions only. The reader used PDF text, renders and hashes without source, research files, literature access or conversation history.

answers.contribution: Global Gaussian comparison plus squared ambient label-distance deficit for every fixed cell count, for a dimension-independent interval near zero.
answers.mechanism: Uniform first-moment localization, exact score-loss normalization, sharp facet cost and aligned covariance contraction, with uniform Hermite control of the rest.
answers.hardest_step: Proposition 5.1, pages 6–7, obtaining limiting measurable facet densities with sharp cost (14). Lemma 3.1 and Proposition 6.1 convert this into the local bound.
answers.limitations: Qualitative constants depending on cell count; balanced Gaussian setting; the whole positive correlation interval is outside the proof.
answers.verification_obstacles: Milman–Neeman and Prékopa are stated and applied by reference. The manuscript gives the Zhang covariance argument and uses no repository input. Priority cannot be determined from the PDF.
